claims.text: Reversal in gen: use the drug's specific reversal agent; if it = unavailable or ineffective, give clotting factors, typically 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC) or sometimes FFP
claims.quote: Many of the anticoagulants have specific reversal agents. If these are unavailable or ineffective, clotting factors, typically in the form of 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate or sometimes fresh frozen plasma, can be given.

claims.text: Heparin: protamine; it works better on unfractionated heparin (UFH) than on LMWH, which it only partly neutralizes
claims.quote: With the heparins, bleeding can be stopped or slowed with protamine (3). It is more effective on unfractionated heparin (UFH) than on low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) because protamine only partially neutralizes LMWH inactivation of factor Xa.

claims.text: During protamine: watch for hypotension and an anaphylaxis-like rxn
claims.quote: During all infusions, patients should be observed for hypotension and a reaction similar to an anaphylactic reaction.

claims.text: Protamine timing: IV UFH has a ½ life of 30 to 60 minutes, so protamine USU isn't given if UFH was received > 60 to 120 minutes earlier, or = given @ a ↓dose
claims.quote: Because UFH given IV has a half-life of 30 to 60 minutes, protamine is typically not given to patients who have received UFH > 60 to 120 minutes beforehand) or is given at a reduced dose based on the amount of heparin estimated to be remaining in plasma, based on the half-life of UFH.

claims.text: Warfarin: reverse w vit K; for severe hemorrhage give PCC, or FFP if PCC = unavailable
claims.quote: Warfarin anticoagulation can be reversed with vitamin K (3). If hemorrhage is severe, prothrombin complex concentrate should be given; fresh frozen plasma may be used if prothrombin complex concentrate is unavailable.

claims.text: INR 5 to 9 w ⍉bleed and ⍉↑bleed risk (selected pts): omit 1 or 2 warfarin doses, check the INR more often, then restart @ a lower dose
claims.quote: Selected patients with overanticoagulation (INR 5 to 9) who are neither actively bleeding nor at increased risk of bleeding can be managed by omitting 1 or 2 warfarin doses and monitoring INR more frequently, then giving warfarin at a lower dose.

claims.text: Dabigatran: idarucizumab; if unavailable, 4-factor PCC; hemodialysis may help; oral activated charcoal if the last dose was w.in 2 hrs
claims.quote: With dabigatran, a humanized monoclonal antibody idarucizumab is an effective antidote to bleeding (3). If the agent is not available, 4-factor prothrombin complex concentratecan be given. Hemodialysis also may help because dabigatran is not highly protein bound. Oral activated charcoal is an option if the last dose of dabigatran was within 2 hours.

claims.text: Oral Xa inhibitors: andexanet alfa (use limited partly by ↑cost); if unavailable, consider 4-factor PCC; oral activated charcoal if taken w.in a few hrs (8 hrs for rivaroxaban, 6 for apixaban, 2 for edoxaban); hemodialysis does ⍉remove them
claims.quote: With factor Xa inhibitors, andexanet alfa is an antidote available in the United States; however, its use is restricted in part due to its high cost (3, 4). Fondaparinux anticoagulation can theoretically also be reversed with andexanet alfa although this has not been studied in research trials. If andexanet alfa is unavailable, 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate may be considered. Oral activated charcoal is an option in patients who took an oral factor Xa inhibitor within a few hours of presentation (8 hours for rivaroxaban, 6 hours for apixaban, and 2 hours for edoxaban). Hemodialysis is not effective for removal of the oral factor Xa inhibitors.

claims.text: PCC: four-factor = preferred over 3-factor; typical dose 50 units/kg IV; reserve it for life-threatening bleed ← its clotting risk
claims.quote: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate is preferred as it tends to be more effective at reversing bleeding than the 3-factor form (3, 5). If 3-factor prothrombin complex concentrate is used, fresh frozen plasma can also be given because fresh frozen plasma contains factor VII. Typical dose is 50 units/kg IV. Because evidence of benefit is uncertain and risk of clotting is significant, prothrombin complex concentrates should be reserved for life-threatening bleeding.

claims.text: FFP: has all clotting factors, but only @ norm plasma levels; used only if PCC = unavailable; ⍉evidence it helps bleed from Xa inhibitors
claims.quote: Fresh frozen plasma contains all the clotting factors but only at normal plasma levels. It is typically used only if prothrombin complex concentrate is unavailable; there is no evidence it is effective in bleeding due to factor Xa inhibitors (3).
